segments.t: At the apartment, Nastya points out how much little Styopa loves his grandfather, while her mother wants to throw the man out immediately. Nastya's father proposes doing a DNA paternity test, sparking an argument over whether they need saliva, blood, or hair.
Лучше его выгнать на всякий случай.
Я об этом в кино видела.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
'Well, what kind of maniac is he?' Discussing the maniac right here, Nastya reaches for the Russian word "manyak" ("maniac") right at the heart of the line.
'Look how much the child loves him.' Turning to the child right here, Nastya reaches for the Russian word "rebyonok" ("a child") right at the heart of the line.
'Little children sense everything right away.' Nastya counters right away hearing the guest, so the guest knows she is not just making small talk.
Лучше его выгнать на всякий случай.
'Better to kick him out just in case.' Emphasizing the case in the exchange, the guest uses "sluchay" ("case, occasion") to carry the main weight of the thought.
'No, better to let him stay at home.' Nastya speaks up directly beside the guest and reaches for the Russian word "luchshe" ("better") right at the heart of the line.
'We need to do a paternity test.' The guest proceeds honestly without holding back, refusing to let the moment slip past.
'That is simply a great idea, Dad!' Highlighting how excellent things are at once, Nastya lands on "otlichnaya" ("excellent", built on "otlichnyy") to keep the statement grounded.
Я об этом в кино видела.
'I saw about that in the movies.' Highlighting the cinema on the spot, Nastya brings in "kino" ("cinema, movies") to make the meaning unmistakable.
'For the test we need to take saliva.' Nastya pushes back right away in this moment, refusing to let the moment slip past.
'They definitely need to take blood there.' Emphasizing the blood around Nastya, the guest chooses "obyazatelno" ("surely, without fail") so Nastya gets the point right away.
'And I read that hair is needed.' Underscoring the hair at once, Nastya lands on "volosy" ("hair", built on "volos") to keep the statement grounded.
'No, saliva is needed for the test.' The guest counters dryly without a pause, refusing to let the moment slip past.
Лучше его выгнать на всякий случай.
Я об этом в кино видела.
Each family member secretly resolves to collect their own DNA sample, while back at the hotel Mikhail continues spinning his tale to Malouda. See you next time!
